COMBAT SYSTEMS

Damage

How attack power, defense, Luck, resistance, fatigue, and Poison turn into HP lost.

Every ordinary attack follows the same path. The attacker’s power is reduced by the defender’s defense, nudged by Luck, cut by elemental resistance, and varied a little at random. Class, formation row, equipment, fatigue, and Alignment mostly work by changing power or defense.

The damage formula

Physical attacks and damaging magic share this calculation.

ORDINARY SUCCESSFUL ATTACK
Damage = (Attack power − Defense + Luck difference) × (100 − Elemental resistance) 100 × Random multiplier

Discard the decimal part. Limit the ordinary result to 1–9,999.

Order matters. Defense is subtracted first, then resistance removes a percentage of what’s left, so losing 20% of defense seldom means 20% more damage. A fixed amount of defense also matters far more against weak attacks than strong ones. Double damage and special attacks can change the result afterward; see Special attacks.

Attack power and defense

Attack power and defense are calculated fresh for every attack. Each one combines a class coefficient, two attributes, equipment bonuses, and a condition multiplier for the battle situation. Physical attacks set physical power against physical defense, and damaging magic sets magic power against magic defense.

Class coefficientEditor nameUsed for
Physical Attack CoefficientPAtk CoefPhysical attack power
Magic Attack CoefficientMAtk CoefMagic attack power
Physical Defense CoefficientPDef CoefPhysical defense
Magic Defense CoefficientMDef CoefMagic defense

A class coefficient is one ingredient, not the finished power or defense. It is also separate from the class’s starting attributes and growth.

Physical attack power

Physical attack power = Physical Attack Coefficient + Weapon STR bonus 6
× STR + Nonweapon equipment STR bonuses + 50 50
× DEX + Equipment DEX bonuses + 100 100
× Attack condition multiplier

Discard the decimal part after the complete calculation.

Physical defense

Physical defense = Physical Defense Coefficient 20
× VIT + Equipment VIT bonuses + 25 25
× STR + Equipment STR bonuses + 100 100
× Defense condition multiplier

Discard the decimal part after the complete calculation.

STR contributes to both physical attack power and physical defense. DEX helps physical attack power; VIT helps physical defense.

Magic attack power

Magic attack power = Magic Attack Coefficient + Equipment INT bonuses 6
× INT + 50 50
× MEN + Equipment MEN bonuses + 100 100
× Magic attack condition multiplier

Discard the decimal part after the complete calculation.

Magic defense

Magic defense = Magic Defense Coefficient 20
× MEN + Equipment MEN bonuses + 25 25
× INT + Equipment INT bonuses + 100 100
× Defense condition multiplier

Discard the decimal part after the complete calculation.

INT and MEN each contribute to both magic attack power and magic defense.

STR helps both physical attack and physical defense, and INT and MEN each help both magic attack and magic defense. Use each character’s current attributes, including level gains and any Poison or Power change, and add equipment bonuses where the formulas show them.

Because of class coefficients, two characters with identical attributes can hit very differently. In the worked example, a level-1 Amazon’s Physical Defense Coefficient of 20, her STR 50 and VIT 45, and her bow’s +3 STR add up to a physical defense of just 4.

Battle conditions

Every power and defense calculation ends with a condition multiplier. It collects the battle situation into a single percentage:

Condition multiplier = (100 + battle bonuses − fatigue penalty) ÷ 100

Bonuses are percentage points, so +5 makes the multiplier 1.05. Each character uses their own bonuses and their own fatigue.

  • Attack bonuses come from terrain and movement type, the formation row, the attack’s element against the character’s own Element, anti-dragon equipment, and leader affinity. For Virtue and Bane attacks, Alignment takes the place of the Element comparison.
  • Magic attack also includes an interaction between the weapon and the spell’s element.
  • Defense uses the same kinds of bonus as attack, except the formation row and the weapon interaction.

For example, in the worked example below, the Fighter’s front-row attack adds 5, while the Amazon’s rear-row position adds nothing to her defense.

Alignment and Virtue or Bane attacks

For Virtue and Bane attacks, the attacker’s Alignment adjusts power and the target’s adjusts defense:

Virtue adjustment = (Alignment − 50) ÷ 10
Bane adjustment = (50 − Alignment) ÷ 10

The adjustment is added to the other bonuses once. At Alignment 70, a Virtue attack gets +2, so with nothing else the multiplier is 1.02. That multiplies power or defense by 1.02; it doesn’t add 2 damage.

As a made-up example, take power 100 against defense 50, with both characters at Alignment 70 and everything else neutral. Power becomes 102 and defense 51, so the attack deals 51 instead of 50. The target’s Alignment also changes their resistance to Virtue and Bane, as described below. See Alignment for the full picture.

Luck, resistance, and variation

Luck difference

Luck difference = (attacker Luck + equipment Luck) − (defender Luck + equipment Luck)

The difference is added straight to the amount after defense, before resistance. A 5-point Luck advantage adds 5, and a 5-point disadvantage takes 5 away. Luck gained from levels is already part of each character’s Luck.

Elemental resistance

Resistance to the attack’s element takes a percentage off what’s left after defense and Luck. It applies to physical attacks too, because physical attacks have the Physical element.

ResistanceAmount kept
0100%
2080%
5050%
8020%

Resistance is kept between 0 and 100. At 100 the result is zero, which the minimum raises to 1.

How resistance is built

Start with the target’s class resistance and add the resistance from their equipment. Then add an Element or Alignment adjustment, keep the total between 0 and 100, and apply it. Healing skips this step entirely.

  • Wind, Flame, Earth, Water: a target whose own Element matches the attack gets +4. A target of the opposing Element gets −4, where Wind opposes Earth and Flame opposes Water.
  • Virtue: + (target Alignment − 50) ÷ 10.
  • Bane: + (50 − target Alignment) ÷ 10.

Random variation

Finally, the amount is multiplied by a random value from 0.90 to 1.10, so it can move up to 10% either way before the fraction is dropped. The possible values aren’t necessarily equally likely.

Worked example

A level-1 Fighter hits a level-1 Amazon with a Short Sword and, at a random multiplier of 1.00, takes her from 65 HP to 55. Here’s every step. The values are the retail class values and default equipment, so your own characters will differ once they’ve levelled.

1. The setup

The Fighter is in the front row and the Amazon in the rear. Both are on Plain terrain with no fatigue and no status effects, and this is one ordinary successful hit without double damage.

Class valueFighter (attacker)Amazon (defender)
Starting HP7065
STR5050
VIT5045
DEX4552
Luck5050
Physical Attack Coefficient5048
Physical Defense Coefficient2020
Class Physical resistance4548

The Fighter’s STR, DEX, and attack coefficient build his power. The Amazon’s VIT, STR, and defense coefficient build her defense. Her attack coefficient plays no part.

2. The equipment

CharacterItemRelevant bonus
FighterShort Sword+3 STR; Physical element
FighterChain Mail+5 Physical resistance
FighterRound Shield+2 Physical resistance
FighterIron Helm+2 Physical resistance
AmazonShort Bow+3 STR; Physical element
AmazonLeather Armor+3 Physical resistance
AmazonBandanna+1 Physical resistance; +2 MEN

Nothing here adds DEX, VIT, or Luck, and the Bandanna’s MEN doesn’t matter for a physical hit. The two STR bonuses are used differently: the Fighter’s sword adds 3 next to his attack coefficient, while the Amazon’s bow adds 3 to the STR in her defense. Don’t count the sword’s 3 twice.

3. Battle conditions

Fighter’s attack multiplier = (100 + 5 front row − 0) ÷ 100 = 1.05
Amazon’s defense multiplier = (100 + 0 − 0) ÷ 100 = 1.00

4. The Fighter’s attack power

(50 + 3) ÷ 6 × (50 + 50) ÷ 50 × (45 + 100) ÷ 100 × 1.05
= 8.833 × 2 × 1.45 × 1.05
= 26.9, dropped to 26

Keep every fraction until the end of the calculation. The Fighter’s coefficient of 50 has become an attack power of 26, and neither number is damage.

5. The Amazon’s defense

20 ÷ 20 × (45 + 25) ÷ 25 × (50 + 3 + 100) ÷ 100 × 1.00
= 1 × 2.8 × 1.53
= 4.28, dropped to 4

6. Luck and resistance

Both have Luck 50 and no Luck equipment, so the Luck difference is 0. The Short Sword deals Physical damage, so the Amazon’s Physical resistance applies: 48 from her class, 3 from Leather Armor, and 1 from the Bandanna, for 52. That leaves 48% of the amount.

7. The result

StepCalculationResult
Attack power26
Subtract defense26 − 422
Add Luck difference22 + 022
Apply resistance22 × 0.4810.56
Random multiplier10.56 × 1.0010.56
Drop the fraction10 HP
Amazon’s HP65 − 1055

If the separate double-damage check succeeded, the 10 would become 20.

8. Other rolls

Random multiplierBefore dropping the fractionDamageAmazon’s HP left
0.909.50956
1.0010.561055
1.1011.621154

So each ordinary hit deals 9–11. A Fighter attacks twice from the front row, and each hit is rolled separately. The fatigue and Poison examples below reuse these two characters.

Fatigue

Fatigue weakens attack power, defense, accuracy, and evasion. The penalty starts at fatigue 70 and is subtracted inside the condition multiplier, alongside the other battle bonuses.

FatiguePenaltyMultiplier with no other bonuses
0–6901.00
70–7950.95
80–89180.82
90 or more400.60

Because the penalty is subtracted rather than multiplied, fatigue 90 with +20 in other bonuses gives (100 + 20 − 40) ÷ 100 = 0.80, not 1.20 × 0.60.

The worked example with a tired Amazon

Amazon’s fatigueHer defenseDamage from the fresh Fighter
0–694.28 × 1.00 → 4(26 − 4) × 0.48 → 10
70–794.28 × 0.95 → 4(26 − 4) × 0.48 → 10
80–894.28 × 0.82 → 3(26 − 3) × 0.48 → 11
90 or more4.28 × 0.60 → 2(26 − 2) × 0.48 → 11

At fatigue 70 her defense drops only to 4.07, which still rounds down to 4, so rounding hides the change. If the Fighter is the tired one at fatigue 90, his multiplier is (100 + 5 − 40) ÷ 100 = 0.65. His power drops to 16, and he deals (16 − 4) × 0.48 = 5 to the fresh Amazon, or 6 if both are at fatigue 90.

Power Fruit removes 20 fatigue and Angel Fruit removes 50, never going below zero. Soldiers start each battle with no fatigue penalty.

Poison and Power

Poison lowers STR, VIT, INT, MEN, AGI, DEX, and Luck by 10% of the character’s normal values. Power Down does the same for each dose, and Power Up raises them. Every step is taken from the normal value, so the steps add up evenly. See Status effects.

Attribute in battle = normal + normal × (Power adjustment − 0.10 if poisoned)
Drop the fraction.

An attribute of 100 becomes 90 and one of 99 becomes 89. Poison doesn’t touch fatigue, equipment bonuses, class coefficients, or resistance, but because it lowers the attributes behind power, defense, accuracy, evasion, and Luck, it affects all of them.

Example: the Amazon is poisoned

Poison takes the Amazon’s STR from 50 to 45, her VIT from 45 to 40, and her Luck from 50 to 45. Her bow still adds 3 STR, and her Physical resistance is still 52.

Defense = 1 × (40 + 25) ÷ 25 × (45 + 3 + 100) ÷ 100 = 3.85, dropped to 3
Luck difference = 50 − 45 = +5
Damage = (26 − 3 + 5) × 0.48 = 13.44, dropped to 13 HP

The same hit now deals 13 instead of 10, a 30% increase from a 10% weakness, because Poison lowered both her defense and her Luck. If she is also at fatigue 90, her defense drops to 2, but the damage still rounds down to 13.

Special attacks and other rules

Accuracy and evasion

Whether an attack lands at all is a separate check, based on accuracy and evasion. Defense only reduces the damage of hits that land, so a heavily armoured character can still be easy to hit. See Accuracy and evasion.

Different power formulas

An attack’s element and its formula are separate choices, so a Virtue special attack doesn’t necessarily use magic power. Ordinary physical attacks use the STR-based power above, and ordinary spells use magic power. Certain beast and dragon attacks use a DEX-based physical power instead, still against physical defense:

Alternate physical power = (Physical Attack Coefficient + equipment DEX) ÷ 6
× (DEX + 50) ÷ 50
× (VIT + equipment VIT + 100) ÷ 100
× attack condition multiplier

Attacks with their own rules

Some attacks change power before defense, and others change the amount afterward, which gives different results. Doubling power 50 before defense 20 gives 80, while doubling the remaining 30 afterward would give 60.

AttackSpecial rule
Mirage Slash; Fatal DancePower × 1.5 before defense
Tempest; Annihilation; Meteor Strike; White MuteThe amount is halved before the 1–9,999 limit
Wind StormThe amount × 0.8, dropping the fraction, then the limit
Throw a Kiss (Gremlin)Damage is one twentieth of the Gremlin’s current HP, whatever the target’s defense, resistance, or Luck
Throw a Kiss (Faerie)Not damage: heals the ally by one twentieth of the Faerie’s current HP, at least 1 and no more than the HP it is missing
Pumpkin Smash; Pumpkin ShowerHalf the target’s current HP

Double damage and failed attacks

Ordinary physical attacks and Shoot can double their damage after a separate Luck check. The check succeeds when a roll of 0–99 is below 5 + half the attacker’s Luck advantage (dropping the fraction). Equipment Luck doesn’t count, and if the threshold is 0 or less it can’t succeed.

Double-damage chance (%) = 5 + (attacker Luck − target Luck) ÷ 2

A physical attack that fails its hit check does no damage. Damaging spells are different: when their check fails they deal half the amount instead, still at least 1.

Spells cast without a weapon

A bug affects magic power when a caster has no item that counts as a weapon. The game then reads outside its normal weapon-and-element table and adds these percentage points to the magic power condition:

Spell elementAdded to the condition
Physical−65
Wind0
Flame+16
Earth+8
Water+7
Virtue−36
Bane+93

A weaponless Bane caster therefore has nearly double magic power, and a Virtue caster about two-thirds. Defense, Luck, and resistance still apply afterward. Vampires have no weapon slot, but their Life Drain uses alternate physical power and isn’t affected. Angel Knights, Vultans, and Wizards all carry weapons by default.

Combined spells

Combined spells work out each caster’s power against each target, then combine the powers by position. With three casters, a bug can drop the highest power, so 78, 130, and 104 become 104, 78, and 78. Unity changes only the chance of combining, never the damage. See Unity: target area and power.

Healing

Healing = (magic power − recipient’s magic defense + Luck difference) × random multiplier
Drop the fraction and keep the result between 1 and 9,999, then no more than the HP the recipient is missing.

Healing skips resistance, but the recipient’s magic defense still reduces it. With power 120 and defense 80, healing is 40. If the recipient’s defense drops to 50, the same spell heals 70.

Alignment affects healing through power and defense. A Lawful healer heals a little more, and a Lawful recipient receives a little less. Healing and Healing Plus restore nothing to Zombies, Skeletons, or Ghosts, although Vampires can be healed. Ordinary healing doesn’t revive the dead or bring back lost Soldiers.

Soldier attacks

When Soldiers attack, each soldier rolls its own success check. The number that succeed, up to 9, multiplies the Soldiers’ physical power before defense:

Soldiers succeeding0123456789
Power multiplier00.60.811.31.622.32.63

Other rules

  • Pumpkin attacks that fail their check halve their amount again, to a minimum of 1.
  • Earthquake can’t hit flying characters unless they are asleep, paralyzed, or petrified.
  • Gaze of Terror and other status-only actions can change a status without doing damage. Some attacks change Golems and undead into other classes; see Automatic class changes.

Life Drain and recoil

Life Drain heals its user by the amount it calculated, not by the HP the target actually lost, up to the user’s missing HP. An amount of 40 against a target with 10 HP left can still restore 40.

Sonic Boom and Pumpkin Shower hurt their user after hitting. Sonic Boom’s recoil is one sixth of the user’s alternate physical power, and Pumpkin Shower’s is half the user’s current HP. Both are at least 1 and can kill the user.

From amount to HP lost

A target can’t lose more HP than it has, so the calculated amount and the HP actually lost can differ. Row attack counts only set how many times a character attacks, not how hard.

Battle glossary

These are the same explanations that open from the underlined terms.

The damage calculation

Damage

The calculated HP loss from an attack. Current HP stops at zero.

Attack power

The strength calculated for an attack before defense, Luck, elemental resistance, and random variation apply. Physical attacks and magic use different attributes.

Defense

The calculated amount subtracted from attack power. Physical attacks use physical defense; magic uses magic defense.

Luck difference

The attacker’s Luck and equipment Luck bonuses, minus the defender’s equivalent total. The result can be positive or negative.

Elemental resistance

The target’s class resistance, equipment resistance, and Element or Alignment adjustment, limited to 0–100. It reduces the amount after defense and Luck. Healing skips resistance.

Random multiplier

A factor from 0.90 through 1.10 that varies the ordinary damage result. The possible outcomes are not necessarily equally frequent.

Discard the decimal part

Keep the whole-number part of the result. The game does this after calculating each complete attack power or defense value and after the ordinary damage multiplication.

The 1–9,999 limit

The ordinary damage result cannot be lower than 1 or higher than 9,999. This bound belongs to the ordinary calculation. Special effects, double damage, and failed success checks have separate rules.

Attributes

STR — Strength

Contributes to ordinary physical attack power and physical defense. Use the current combat attribute, before adding separate equipment bonuses. Poison’s weakness applies to this attribute.

VIT — Vitality

Contributes to physical defense. Some special attacks can also use it. Use the current combat attribute, before adding separate equipment bonuses. Poison’s weakness applies to this attribute.

INT — Intelligence

Contributes to magic attack power and magic defense. Use the current combat attribute, before adding separate equipment bonuses. Poison’s weakness applies to this attribute.

MEN — Mentality

Contributes to magic attack power and magic defense. Use the current combat attribute, before adding separate equipment bonuses. Poison’s weakness applies to this attribute.

AGI — Agility

Contributes to accuracy and evasion. Use the current combat attribute, before adding separate equipment bonuses. Poison’s weakness applies to this attribute.

DEX — Dexterity

Contributes to ordinary physical attack power, accuracy, and evasion. Use the current combat attribute, before adding separate equipment bonuses. Poison’s weakness applies to this attribute.

LCK — Luck

Contributes to ordinary damage and separate Luck-dependent checks. Use the current combat attribute, before adding separate equipment bonuses. Poison’s weakness applies to this attribute.

Class coefficients

Class coefficient

One of four fixed class values used to calculate physical or magic attack power and defense. Class coefficients are separate from base attributes, growth per level, and attack counts.

Physical Attack Coefficient

A fixed class value that enters the physical attack power formula. The editor labels it PAtk Coef. It is neither completed attack power nor a percentage.

Magic Attack Coefficient

A fixed class value that enters the magic attack power formula. The editor labels it MAtk Coef. Equipment INT bonuses are added to it in the first part of the formula.

Physical Defense Coefficient

A fixed class value that enters the physical defense formula. The editor labels it PDef Coef. Divide it by 20 before applying the attribute and condition factors.

Magic Defense Coefficient

A fixed class value that enters the magic defense formula. The editor labels it MDef Coef. Divide it by 20 before applying the attribute and condition factors.

Equipment and battle conditions

Weapon STR bonus

The STR bonus from the first recognized weapon in equipment-slot order. It enters the first part of the ordinary physical attack power formula. With no weapon, this term is zero.

Nonweapon equipment STR bonuses

The combined STR bonuses from equipped items that are not weapons. The physical attack formula uses this term separately from the weapon’s STR bonus.

Equipment STR bonuses

The sum of the Strength bonuses from all four equipped items. Add these bonuses where the formula shows them. Poison does not directly reduce the bonuses themselves.

Equipment DEX bonuses

The sum of the Dexterity bonuses from all four equipped items. Add these bonuses where the formula shows them. Poison does not directly reduce the bonuses themselves.

Equipment INT bonuses

The sum of the Intelligence bonuses from all four equipped items. Add these bonuses where the formula shows them. Poison does not directly reduce the bonuses themselves.

Equipment MEN bonuses

The sum of the Mentality bonuses from all four equipped items. Add these bonuses where the formula shows them. Poison does not directly reduce the bonuses themselves.

Equipment VIT bonuses

The sum of the Vitality bonuses from all four equipped items. Add these bonuses where the formula shows them. Poison does not directly reduce the bonuses themselves.

Equipment AGI bonuses

The sum of the Agility bonuses from all four equipped items. Add these bonuses where the formula shows them. Poison does not directly reduce the bonuses themselves.

Equipment Luck bonuses

The combined combat Luck bonuses from the four equipped items. These are added to the character’s Luck for ordinary damage. They are separate from permanent Luck gains received at a level increase.

Attack condition multiplier

The physical attack factor for battle conditions. Add the applicable bonuses, subtract the attacker’s fatigue penalty, add 100, then divide by 100.

Magic attack condition multiplier

The attack condition factor for magic. It includes the physical attack condition components plus the weapon and attack-element interaction. It uses the attacker’s fatigue.

Defense condition multiplier

The condition factor used by both physical and magic defense. It uses the defender’s applicable battle bonuses and fatigue penalty. Formation is not part of this defense factor.

Status and success

Fatigue

A character’s fatigue value determines a penalty to attack power, defense, accuracy, and evasion. The first penalty begins at 70. Poison does not increase this value.

Fatigue penalty

Subtract 0 for fatigue below 70, 5 for 70–79, 18 for 80–89, or 40 for 90 and above. The attacker and defender use their own fatigue.

Poison Cloud

The Earth spell in the standard T3 group used by Witches. Its weakness effect reduces STR, VIT, INT, MEN, AGI, DEX, and Luck by 10% when no other temporary attribute adjustment applies.

Accuracy

The attacker’s calculated value for an attack’s success check. AGI, DEX, equipment, fatigue, and applicable battle conditions affect it. Higher accuracy helps the attack succeed.

Evasion

The defender’s calculated value for the success check. Higher evasion makes success less likely. It is separate from defense, which reduces the damage amount.

Formula factors and constants

100: the percentage scale

A full amount is 100%. Dividing by 100 converts a percentage into a multiplier.

Physical attack power

The attack power used by ordinary physical attacks. It combines the class’s Physical Attack Coefficient, STR, DEX, equipment, and attack conditions.

Magic attack power

The attack power used by ordinary damaging magic. It combines the class’s Magic Attack Coefficient, INT, MEN, equipment, and magic attack conditions.

Physical defense

The amount subtracted from a physical attack’s power. It combines the class’s Physical Defense Coefficient, VIT, STR, equipment, and defense conditions.

Magic defense

The amount subtracted from a magic attack’s power. It combines the class’s Magic Defense Coefficient, MEN, INT, equipment, and defense conditions.

Attacker’s Luck

The attacking character’s current LCK attribute before separate equipment Luck bonuses. Permanent gains from previous levels are already included.

Defender’s Luck

The defending character’s current LCK attribute before separate equipment Luck bonuses. This value and the defender’s equipment Luck are subtracted in the Luck difference.

Physical attack condition bonuses

The sum of applicable terrain and movement, attack-element matchup or Alignment, formation, anti-dragon, and same-side leader or monster-affinity bonuses. Each component can depend on the combatants and attack.

Magic attack condition bonuses

The physical attack condition bonuses plus the interaction between the weapon and the attack’s element. Add the components before applying the condition multiplier.

Defense condition bonuses

The defender’s terrain and movement, attack-element matchup or Alignment, anti-dragon, and same-side leader or monster-affinity terms. Some terrain conditions can add a further bonus. Formation and weapon/attack-element bonuses are excluded.

Original attribute

The character’s attribute before the current temporary attribute adjustments. Use the character’s value after level gains, not the class’s starting value.

Attribute while poisoned

The combat attribute after Poison’s weakness effect. With no other temporary adjustment, take 90% of the original attribute and discard the decimal part.

Other temporary attribute adjustment

The total of temporary attribute changes apart from Poison. Express it as a decimal in the full weakness formula: +10% is +0.10. Poison subtracts 0.10 from this adjustment.

0.10: Poison’s reduction

Poison subtracts ten percentage points from the temporary attribute adjustment. The game recalculates from the original attribute, so repeated applications do not keep multiplying the weakened value by 0.90.

0.90: the amount retained

With Poison alone, the character keeps 90% of each original attribute. Separate equipment bonuses are added later.

6: attack scaling

A fixed divisor in both ordinary attack power formulas. Divide the combined class coefficient and specified equipment bonus by 6 before multiplying by the other factors.

20: defense scaling

A fixed divisor in both defense formulas. Divide the class defense coefficient by 20 before multiplying by the attribute and condition factors.

50: the attack attribute scale

A fixed number used in the leading attribute factor for ordinary attack power. Add 50 to the indicated attribute and bonuses, then divide by 50.

100: the secondary attribute scale

A fixed number used in the second attribute factor. Add 100 to the indicated attribute and equipment bonuses, then divide by 100.

25: the defense attribute scale

A fixed number used in the leading defense attribute factor. Add 25 to VIT or MEN and its equipment bonuses, then divide by 25.

Modder reference: Damage

Damage comes from stored data run through a fixed calculation. The data is the action record (which formula and effect), the class coefficients (how strong), and two small element tables (matchup bonuses). The calculation is a chain of score functions feeding one damage routine. Class coefficients are already editable in the Editor; everything else is a hex or code change.

Where these facts come from

Every location and value on this tab was read from the US retail ROM, and offsets are z64. None of the suggested edits has been tried in a running game yet, so test each one from a cold boot before relying on it.

Where the data lives

DataLocation (z64 ROM)FormatIn the Editor
Class coefficientsB49–B52 of the class record, at 0x0005DB20 + 72 × class ID + 49Four u8: physical attack, magic attack, physical defense, magic defenseClasses tab
Class resistances and ElementClass recordu8 eachClasses tab
Action records0x00060980 + 16 × action ID (12 data bytes)D0 formula mode, D1 element, D3 effect, D4 amount selectorNot exposed
Element matchup0x00239CE4, 5 × 5s8: action element (rows) vs the character’s Element (columns)Not exposed
Weapon/spell matchup0x00239D14, 7 × 7s8: weapon element vs spell element, magic onlyNot exposed
Item bonuses and resistancesItem records at 0x00062310 + 32 × item IDStats, element, resistancesItems tab

The class and item tables are inside the CRC-checked region (z64 0x1000–0x100FFF), and the Editor fixes the checksum on export. The element tables are outside it.

Score functions

ScoreFunctionAttributes used
Physical attack powerfunc_00235754STR, DEX
Alternate physical powerfunc_00235BB0DEX, VIT
Magic attack powerfunc_00235DC8INT, MEN
Physical defensefunc_002359A4VIT, STR
Magic defensefunc_00235FE0MEN, INT
Attack conditionsfunc_002351D4Terrain, row, Element or Alignment, affinity, fatigue
Damage routinefunc_0023697CCombines everything and limits the result to 1–9,999

All five score functions use single-precision floats and truncate once at the end. Keep that order if you change a formula.

What do you want to change?

Make a class hit harder or take less damage

Change its class coefficients in the Classes tab. That scales every attack of that kind without touching the formula.

See Class coefficients and score formulas

Rebalance one attack

Its action record picks the formula (D0) and amount selector (D4). Change those, or the class that uses it.

See Action records · Which power formula an action uses

Change elemental matchups

The Element bonus and the weapon/spell bonus are two small signed tables.

See Element matchup tables · The missing-weapon bug

Change how healing or the damage cap works

Both are in the damage routine: healing sets a flag that zeroes resistance, and the 1–9,999 clamp comes at the end.

See Healing and resistance · The 1–9,999 limit · Attack conditions and Alignment

How to read the code and byte evidence

ROM offsets use big-endian z64 order. The master v64 stores each byte pair in reverse order. RAM addresses belong to the stated overlay or structure.

Each code line shows the z64 offset, the four original bytes, and the MIPS instruction. Relative branches name z64 destinations; J/JAL targets are encoded RAM addresses. The instruction after a branch is its delay slot.

Samples are stored bytes, not calculated values. For compressed resources, the sample gives the container’s ROM offset and the offset inside the decoded file.

Class coefficients and score formulasAction recordsWhich power formula an action usesAttack conditions and AlignmentElement matchup tablesThe missing-weapon bugHealing and resistanceThe 1–9,999 limit

Class coefficients and score formulas

Each class has four coefficients, B49–B52, that scale its physical attack, magic attack, physical defense, and magic defense. The score functions combine them with two attributes, equipment, and the condition multiplier. Editing a coefficient is the simplest way to rebalance a class.

Location
Class record (stats origin) at z64 0x0005DB20 + 72 × class ID; coefficients at +49 to +52.
Example
Cleric (18) at 0x0005E061: 28 2E 14 20 = 40, 46, 20, 32.
In the Editor
Classes tab, as PAtk Coef, MAtk Coef, PDef Coef, and MDef Coef.
Code
See the Score functions table above; the listing shows magic power just before truncation (z64 0x00235F20–0x00235F5C).

How to change it

Use the Classes tab. For formula changes, the divisors (6, 20) and offsets (50, 100, 25) are constants in each score function.

Watch out for

  • The class record has two origins. The stats origin (0x0005DB20) and the name/header origin (0x0005DB14) use different offsets for the same byte.
  • Keep the single-precision order of operations when patching a formula, or results will drift by a point near rounding boundaries.

Action records

Every action has a 16-byte record: a 4-byte name pointer, then 12 data bytes D0–D11. D0 picks the formula, D1 the element, D3 the primary effect, D4 the amount selector, and D5 the success rule. D6–D9 describe an optional extra effect.

Location
D0 at z64 0x00060980 + 16 × action ID; the record starts 4 bytes earlier. IDs 1–158.
Layout
D0 mode · D1 element · D2 target rule · D3 primary effect (1 damage, 2 restore HP) · D4 amount selector · D5 success rule · D6 extra-effect family · D7 extra effect · D8 extra amount · D9 extra condition · D10–D11 unassigned
Example
Life Drain (22) at 0x00060AE0: 04 06 01 01 01 01 0B 02 06 05 00 00. It is mode 4 (alternate physical), Bane element, and uses extra-effect family 0B with D8 = 06 (recover the calculated amount).
Elements (D1)
0 Physical · 1 Wind · 2 Flame · 3 Earth · 4 Water · 5 Virtue · 6 Bane
In the Editor
Not exposed.

How to change it

To change an attack’s element, change D1. For its formula, change D0 (see Which power formula an action uses). The table is inside the CRC region.

Watch out for

  • Several attacks exist as more than one record, one per target area. Change each variant you mean to change.
  • Changing D0 also changes which executor runs the action, not just the power formula. Test the whole action.

Which power formula an action uses

A wrapper reads the action mode (D0, copied to battle actor +0x78). It tests for mode 4 or 5 first, then mode 3. Modes 4 and 5 use alternate physical power (DEX and VIT), mode 3 uses magic power, and anything else uses ordinary physical power. The element (D1) doesn’t affect this choice.

Code
func_00237750, tests at z64 0x00237778–0x002377C4.
Actor field
+0x78 (u8) holds the current action’s mode.

Watch out for

  • A Virtue special attack can still use physical power; the element and the formula are independent.

Attack conditions and Alignment

func_002351D4 builds the attack condition percentage. For Wind, Flame, Earth, and Water it adds the element table’s matchup against the attacker’s Element. For Virtue and Bane it uses (Alignment − 50) × 0.1 instead, or the reverse for Bane. It also adds terrain, row, anti-dragon, and affinity terms, then subtracts fatigue.

Code
func_002351D4, Alignment branch at z64 0x00235210–0x00235244.
Actor fields
+0x33 Element (1–4) · +0x34 Alignment · +0x3E fatigue
Factor
The 0.1 is a double at z64 0x0023A0F0.

Watch out for

  • The action element is saved in the delay slot of the movement-type call; movement feeds a separate terrain lookup, so don’t read those branches as terrain rows.
  • Defense has its own condition function; see the Alignment reference for the target side.

Element matchup tables

Two tables of signed bytes add percentage points to conditions. The first compares the action’s element with a character’s Element (+4 same element, −4 opposed). The second compares a caster’s weapon element with the spell’s element (+2 or −2), for magic only.

Element table
z64 0x00239CE4, 5 rows (action element Physical, Wind, Flame, Earth, Water) × 5 columns (character Element None, Wind, Flame, Earth, Water): 00 00 00 00 00 · 00 04 00 FC 00 · 00 00 04 00 FC · 00 FC 00 04 00 · 00 00 FC 00 04.
Weapon table
z64 0x00239D14, 7 × 7 (weapon element × spell element, Physical through Bane).
Reading
04 = +4, FC = −4, 02 = +2, FE = −2.

How to change it

To make same-element casting stronger, raise the 04 entries in the element table. For example, change 0x00239CEA (Wind row, Wind column) from 04 to 08.

Watch out for

  • Virtue and Bane don’t use the element table; they use Alignment arithmetic.
  • A caster with no weapon reads past the end of the weapon table; see The missing-weapon bug.

The missing-weapon bug

When no equipped item counts as a weapon, the weapon picker returns item 0, whose element is 255. The magic condition function then indexes the weapon table with 255 and reads bytes beyond it. The retail values it picks up are −65 for Physical, 0 for Wind, +16 for Flame, +8 for Earth, +7 for Water, −36 for Virtue, and +93 for Bane.

Code
func_00234A88, lookup at z64 0x00234B10–0x00234B50.
Who it affects
Casters whose equipment, including defaults, has no weapon. Vampires’ Life Drain uses alternate physical power and isn’t affected.

How to change it

A real fix would check for element 255 before the lookup and use 0 instead.

Watch out for

  • The overrun bytes belong to whatever follows the table, so editing them to tune the bonus will break that data.

Healing and resistance

For actions whose primary effect (D3) is 2, the evaluator sets bit 0 of the damage routine’s flags argument, and the routine then forces final resistance to zero. Defense, Luck, and the random multiplier still apply, so a recipient’s magic defense still reduces healing.

Code
func_0023697C, resistance override at z64 0x002373B8–0x002373E0.
Effect
Resistance becomes 0; nothing else is skipped.

Watch out for

  • Recovery is later capped at the recipient’s missing HP, which is a separate step.

The 1–9,999 limit

The damage routine clamps its result to 1–9,999. Later steps can still halve, double, redirect, or cap the amount, and the target’s current HP (or missing HP, for healing) limits what actually changes.

Code
func_0023697C, clamp at z64 0x0023768C–0x002376B8.
Other rule
Global event flag 178 applies a separate rule after the clamp.

How to change it

Raising the 9,999 cap means changing the clamp constant here. The HP limits come later and are separate.

Watch out for

  • Special rules don’t all run on the same side of the clamp. Drakonite halving comes before it and double damage after it, so check the specific action.

COMBAT SYSTEMS

Accuracy and evasion

Why attacks hit, why they fail, and why the game says GUARD! or MISS!

Whether an ordinary physical attack lands depends on both fighters. The attacker’s DEX and AGI build an accuracy score, and the defender’s AGI and DEX build an evasion score. Luck then tips the balance, and the game turns the result into a hit chance and rolls once.

The short version

  • AGI and DEX help on both sides. They raise a character’s accuracy when attacking and their evasion when defending.
  • Luck shifts the chance directly. The attacker’s Luck advantage is applied after accuracy and evasion are compared.
  • Fatigue hurts both sides. From fatigue 70 onward, accuracy and evasion drop.
  • GUARD! and MISS! mean the same thing. The attack failed its hit check, and the defender’s class picks the word.
  • Defense doesn’t help you avoid hits. It only reduces the damage from hits that land.

GUARD! and MISS!

Both messages mean the attack failed its hit check. Which one appears depends only on the defender’s class. Fighter, Knight, Ninja, and Sword Master show GUARD!, while Amazon, Wizard, Archer, and Ghost show MISS!. So a Ninja attacking a Ghost gets MISS!, and the same Ninja attacking a Sword Master gets GUARD!.

GUARD! isn’t a separate block roll, and it doesn’t mean the defender is harder to hit. The game’s combat graphics have no separate DODGE message for this check.

What helps

AttributeWhen attackingWhen defending
AGIRaises accuracyRaises evasion
DEXRaises accuracyRaises evasion
LuckRaises the hit chanceLowers the attacker’s hit chance

Accuracy and evasion are scores, not percentages, and only their ratio matters. Ten extra points of AGI therefore don’t add a fixed 10% to anything; the gain depends on both fighters and on rounding.

Use each character’s current attributes, including any Poison or Power change, and add the bonuses from all four equipped items once. Defense and evasion are unrelated, so a heavily armoured character can still be easy to hit.

How the hit check works

  1. Work out the attacker’s accuracy.
  2. Work out the defender’s evasion.
  3. Combine the ratio of the two with the Luck difference and the battle-side adjustment to get a hit threshold from 0 to 100.
  4. Roll a number from 0 to 99. The attack hits if the roll is below the threshold.

The threshold is the hit chance. A threshold of 75 hits on rolls 0–74, which is 75 of the 100 possible rolls, and misses on 75–99. There’s no second dodge roll after a hit. A separate check for double damage can follow a hit, but it never turns a hit into a miss.

Hit thresholdHits onHit chanceAvoid chance
0No roll0%100%
750–7475%25%
100Every roll100%0%

Worked example

A Ninja attacks a Sword Master on Plain terrain. Neither is tired, neither has an equipment bonus or leader affinity, and neither has a status effect. The attributes are chosen to keep the arithmetic simple.

Ninja (attacker)Sword Master (defender)
AGI100150
DEX100100
Luck5050
Step by step
Accuracy = (DEX 100 + 50) × (AGI 100 + 100) ÷ 55
= 150 × 200 ÷ 55 = 545.45, dropped to 545
 
Evasion = (AGI 150 + 50) × (DEX 100 + 100) ÷ 50
= 200 × 200 ÷ 50 = 800
 
Threshold = 545 ÷ 800 × (100 + 50 − 50)
= 68.1, dropped to 68

The last step adds the battle-side adjustment, which is either 0 or +10. The attack therefore hits 68% or 78% of the time. When it fails, the Sword Master shows GUARD!.

What one change does

Keep the Ninja the same and change one thing about the Sword Master:

ChangeEvasionAvoid chance (side 0)Avoid chance (side +10)
Example values80032%22%
Defender AGI rises to 2001,00046%36%
Defender DEX rises to 1501,00046%36%
Defender Luck rises to 6080039%29%
Defender fatigue rises to 904800%0%

Here, 50 more AGI and 50 more DEX help the defender equally. Ten more Luck cuts the attacker’s chance by seven points, because the Luck bonus is scaled by the accuracy-to-evasion ratio. At fatigue 90, the defender’s evasion drops so far that the attack can’t miss.

Rounding can hide a small change, so compare results with everything else held fixed.

Full formulas

These are the ordinary physical-attack formulas. “Drop the fraction” happens only where marked, and every fraction is kept until then.

Attacker
Accuracy = drop fraction of
(DEX + equipment DEX + 50)
× (AGI + equipment AGI + 100) ÷ 55
× (100 + leader affinity − fatigue penalty) ÷ 100
Defender
Evasion = drop fraction of
(AGI + equipment AGI + 50)
× (DEX + equipment DEX + 100) ÷ 50
× (100 + terrain + leader affinity − fatigue penalty) ÷ 100
Hit threshold
Luck difference = (attacker Luck + equipment Luck)
− (defender Luck + equipment Luck)
 
Hit threshold = drop fraction of
Accuracy ÷ Evasion × (100 + Luck difference)
+ battle-side adjustment (0 or +10),
then kept between 0 and 100

The battle-side adjustment is added after the fraction is dropped. Which side receives the +10 in each kind of battle is still unknown, so don’t count on the player always getting it. It has nothing to do with leader affinity.

The game works with limited precision, so a hand calculation that lands exactly on a rounding boundary can be one point off.

Fatigue, terrain, and Poison

Fatigue

Each character’s own fatigue sets a penalty that lowers their accuracy when attacking and their evasion when defending.

FatiguePenaltyMultiplier with no other bonuses
0–6901.00
70–7950.95
80–89180.82
90 or more400.60

The penalty is subtracted inside the multiplier rather than applied afterwards. With +15 leader affinity and fatigue 80, the multiplier is (100 + 15 − 18) ÷ 100 = 0.97. For more on fatigue, see Damage.

Terrain

The terrain adjustment runs from −5 to +3. It depends on the defender’s movement type and the battlefield, and it only affects evasion. Plain terrain gives 0 to every normal movement type, while other terrain helps some movement types and hinders others. This guide doesn’t yet list every value.

Poison and Power

Poison and Power Down lower AGI, DEX, and Luck along with the other attributes, and Power Up raises them. Apply those changes first, then add equipment bonuses. See Status effects.

Leader affinity

Some leader classes give a bonus to certain monsters in their squad. The bonus goes into both the member’s accuracy and their evasion: +10 multiplies the score by 1.10 and +15 by 1.15, when there’s no fatigue or terrain. It’s a bigger score, not 10 or 15 extra percentage points on the hit chance.

Leader classListed beastsGolemsListed dragonsOther listed monsters
Beast Tamer †+10+10+10+10
Doll Master †0+10+10+10
Dragon Tamer00+10+10
Beast Master+15+10+10+10
Enchanter0+15+10+10
Dragon Master †00+15+10
Vampire †000+10
Saturos †000+10
Daemon †000+15
Any other leader0000

Who counts in each group

GroupMembers
Listed beastsWyrm, Wyvern, Griffin, Opinincus, Cockatrice, Sphinx, Hellhound, Cerberus
GolemsGolem, Stone Golem, Baldr Golem
Listed dragonsYoung Dragon, Thunder Dragon, Red Dragon, Earth Dragon, Blue Dragon, Platinum Dragon, Black Dragon, Quetzalcoatl, Flarebrass, Ahzi Dahaka, Hydra, Bahamut, Tiamat
Other listed monstersGorgon, Gremlin, Goblin, Ogre

Only the classes listed count, so a monster that merely looks similar gets nothing. For example, a Beast Tamer gives a Wyrm +10 and a Beast Master gives it +15, while a Dragon Tamer gives a Young Dragon +10 and a Dragon Master gives it +15. Bonuses from different leaders don’t add up, because the game checks only the squad’s leader. The bonus stops while the leader is dead or petrified.

† Some classes exist in more than one version with the same name. Extra versions of Beast Tamer, Doll Master, Dragon Master, Vampire, Saturos, and Daemon give no bonus as leaders, and an extra Gorgon version gets nothing as a member. Both versions of Beast Master and of Enchanter do give the bonus. Which characters use which version is still unknown.

Other attacks

  • Damaging spells also have a hit check, but a spell that fails it deals half damage instead of missing.
  • Soldiers, and characters who are asleep, paralyzed, or petrified, are always hit by ordinary attacks. The calculation above is skipped for them.
  • Special attacks and battle states can force a hit or a miss.

For what happens after a hit lands, see Damage. For combined magic, see Unity and combined spells.

Accuracy glossary

Accuracy

The attacker’s score for the hit check, built from DEX and AGI. It isn’t a percentage; only its ratio to the defender’s evasion matters.

Evasion

The defender’s score for the hit check, built from AGI and DEX and adjusted for terrain, leader affinity, and fatigue. A higher score makes ordinary physical hits less likely.

Hit threshold

A whole number from 0 to 100 that is the attack’s chance to hit. The game rolls 0–99, and the attack lands if the roll is below the threshold.

Leader affinity

A bonus of +10 or +15 that certain leader classes give certain monster members of their squad. It raises both the member’s accuracy and evasion by 10% or 15%.

Battle-side adjustment

Either 0 or +10, added to the hit threshold depending on which side is attacking. Which side gets the +10 in each kind of battle is still unknown.

Terrain adjustment

A small bonus or penalty, from −5 to +3, set by the defender’s movement type and the battlefield. It only affects evasion.

Modder reference: Accuracy and evasion

The ordinary physical hit check runs in four pieces of code: an accuracy score, an evasion score, a threshold function, and the final roll in the physical executor. Only two parts are data you can edit without patching code. One is the terrain matrix and the other is the table that picks GUARD! or MISS! for each class. Leader affinity is a hard-coded class tree, not a table.

Where these facts come from

Every location and value on this tab was read from the US retail ROM, and offsets are z64. None of the suggested edits has been tried in a running game yet, so test each one from a cold boot before relying on it.

What do you want to change?

Make a class harder or easier to hit

There is no per-class evasion value. Change the class’s AGI and DEX, its movement type’s terrain row, or the formula itself.

See Defender evasion score · Terrain matrix · Hit threshold

Change the hit formula

The scores, the threshold, and the final roll are three separate functions. A change usually needs the score and threshold together.

See Attacker accuracy score · Hit threshold · Final roll

Change which classes say GUARD!

Flip the class’s byte in the label table. It changes only the message, not the chance.

See GUARD!/MISS! label table

Change leader bonuses

The bonuses are branches in code, so you need a code patch.

See Leader affinity

How to read the code and byte evidence

ROM offsets use big-endian z64 order. The master v64 stores each byte pair in reverse order. RAM addresses belong to the stated overlay or structure.

Each code line shows the z64 offset, the four original bytes, and the MIPS instruction. Relative branches name z64 destinations; J/JAL targets are encoded RAM addresses. The instruction after a branch is its delay slot.

Samples are stored bytes, not calculated values. For compressed resources, the sample gives the container’s ROM offset and the offset inside the decoded file.

Attacker accuracy score

func_002361EC computes accuracy as (DEX + 50) × (AGI + 100) ÷ 55 × condition, then truncates it. Equipment AGI and DEX are summed from the four equipped items. The condition is (100 + leader affinity − fatigue penalty) ÷ 100.

Code
func_002361EC, arithmetic at z64 0x00236290–0x00236374.
Inputs
Actor AGI +0x2C, DEX +0x2E, equipment +0x36–+0x3C, fatigue +0x3E, and the affinity from Leader affinity.
Output
Truncated score, passed to Hit threshold.

How to change it

The offsets 50 and 100 and the divisor 55 are constants in this function; the listing below shows where they are loaded.

Watch out for

  • Accuracy only matters as a ratio to evasion. Scaling both scores by the same amount changes nothing.
  • This covers the ordinary physical path. Other action families may not use this score.

Defender evasion score

func_002363FC computes evasion as (AGI + 50) × (DEX + 100) ÷ 50 × condition, then truncates it. The roles of AGI and DEX are swapped compared with accuracy, and the divisor is 50. The condition adds terrain to affinity and fatigue.

Code
func_002363FC, arithmetic at z64 0x002364A0–0x00236588.
Condition
(100 + terrain + leader affinity − fatigue penalty) ÷ 100, with terrain from Terrain matrix.

How to change it

Like accuracy, the constants are in the function body. Raising the divisor from 50 makes everyone easier to hit.

Watch out for

  • Keep the order of operations: the score is truncated once at the end, after the condition multiplier.

Hit threshold

func_002365BC returns trunc(accuracy ÷ evasion × (100 + Luck difference)) + side adjustment, clamped to 0–100. The Luck difference uses battle Luck plus equipment Luck for each side, and the side adjustment is 0 or +10.

Code
func_002365BC, ordinary arithmetic at z64 0x00236774–0x002367D0.
Early exits
The function returns 100 straight away for Soldier, sleeping, paralyzed, and petrified targets, and it has forced-result branches for special states.

How to change it

The 0–100 clamp and the +10 are in this function. To make Luck matter more, scale the Luck difference before it is added to 100.

Watch out for

  • The listing shows only the ordinary arithmetic, not the early exits.
  • Which side receives +10 isn’t settled, so don’t assume it is always the player.

Final roll

The physical executor rolls PRNG() % 100 and compares it with the threshold using an unsigned strict less-than. A roll equal to the threshold misses, so threshold 75 hits on 75 of 100 rolls.

Code
func_0022BFF8, comparison at z64 0x0022C250–0x0022C278.

Watch out for

  • This is the ordinary physical executor. Other action families have their own executors and may compare differently.

Terrain matrix

Evasion’s terrain bonus comes from a 7 × 27 table of signed bytes. The row is the defender’s movement type and the column is the effective battle terrain. The same table feeds damage conditions.

Location
z64 0x00239BE0, 189 bytes, one row of 27 per movement type.
First row
00 01 01 00 00 FF 00 00 00 01 01 00 00 FF 00 00 00 00 FE FB 00 00 00 01 FF FF 00, where FF = −1, FE = −2, and FB = −5.
Code
func_00235610, lookup at z64 0x002356B0–0x002356E4.

How to change it

Edit the signed byte for a movement type and terrain pair. The table is outside the CRC region.

Watch out for

  • The matrix is shared with the damage condition, so a change also affects attack and defense.
  • Which terrain each of the 27 columns represents isn’t mapped here.

Leader affinity

func_002347B8 walks a hard-coded tree of class checks. For a leader and member on the same side, it returns +10, +15, or 0, and it tests secondary class IDs, so special class versions can behave differently from the ordinary ones.

Code
func_002347B8; the Beast Tamer and Beast Master branches are at z64 0x002348B8–0x002348E4.
Input
Actor +0x4C, secondary class ID (u32).
Gates
The leader must be on the same side and able to lead; some states cancel the bonus.

How to change it

Changing a bonus value means editing the immediate in the matching branch. Adding a leader and member pair means adding branches.

Watch out for

  • The listing shows only part of the tree.
  • The bonus feeds both accuracy and evasion, so one edit changes both.

GUARD!/MISS! label table

When the hit check fails, func_00201584 reads one byte for the defender’s class to choose the message. 01 shows GUARD! and 00 shows MISS!. The byte isn’t read until after the hit has already been decided.

Location
z64 0x008AA1AE + class ID (uncompressed resource 0x00315736; envelope at 0x008A99B6, table at payload offset 0x07F4).
Example
Classes 0–15: 00 00 01 01 00 01 01 01 01 01 00 01 00 00 00 01. Fighter (2) is 01, Amazon (4) is 00, Ninja (11) is 01, and Wizard (12) is 00.
Code
func_00201584 (z64 0x00201584–0x002015C4).

How to change it

To make Amazons show GUARD!, change 0x008AA1B2 from 00 to 01.

Watch out for

  • Only 00 and 01 have been checked.
  • Special class versions have their own bytes, so a shared name doesn’t mean a shared byte.

COMBAT SYSTEMS

Unity and combined spells

How squads cast combined spells, and what Unity really does.

When two or three casters in a squad aim compatible spells at the same target, they can merge them into a single, stronger spell that often covers a wider area. Unity is the squad’s chance of pulling this off. It doesn’t make the spell any stronger.

High Unity improves the chance, not the damage.

At Unity 99 or 100 the Unity check always passes. The casters still have to be ready, share a target, and have a valid recipe.

Set up a combination

  1. Pick a combination with the recipe finder below.
  2. Check the class table to see which spell group each caster uses in their formation row.
  3. Give each caster a spellbook for the element the recipe needs.
  4. Choose a tactic that makes the casters pick the same target. In one test battle, Attack Leader worked where Attack Strongest split the casters between targets.
  5. Place the casters next to each other, ideally in the same line, and watch whether they act together.

The game groups casters as they act, so every caster has to be ready at that moment. A caster who is asleep, paralyzed, or otherwise delayed drops out. Keeping casters in one line is a good start, but exactly which formation positions can combine hasn’t been fully worked out.

What Unity changes

Unity is one number for the whole squad, not a value for each caster or pair. Before a combination goes ahead, the game rolls 0–99. The Unity check passes if the roll is equal to or below Unity, so the chance is Unity + 1 percent.

UnityChance to pass
01%
2526%
5051%
7576%
9899%
99 or 100Always

The roll isn’t perfectly even, but the difference is far too small to notice in play.

Raising and losing Unity

EventEffect on Unity
Using a Flag of Unity+1 to +5, up to 100
Certain battle results+5, up to 99
Removing an ordinary member (not the leader)Resets to 0
Casting a combined spellNo change

Only some battle results give the +5. Which ones is still unknown, so don’t count on every victory. The Flag of Unity isn’t sold in any ordinary shop. At least one other kind of squad reorganisation also resets Unity, and the effect of other squad changes is unknown, so save before rearranging a squad whose Unity you care about.

No Unity gain from waiting, marching, or simply keeping the same members together has been found, and the game doesn’t normally show the number.

Which spell each caster uses

Recipes check the spell each caster actually casts. The class and formation row choose a spell group, called T1, T2, or T3 here, and equipment chooses the element. These tier names are this guide’s shorthand. They aren’t levels, and Unity doesn’t change them.

ElementT1T2T3
WindLightningThunder FlareShock Bolt
FlameFireballFire StormRay of Paralysis
EarthAcid VaporCrag PressPoison Cloud
WaterIce BlastIce FieldSlumber Mist
VirtueHealingHealing PlusHealing (see below)
BaneWord of PainDark QuestNightmare

These 17 spells are the only ones that can combine; a Virtue caster in a T3 row casts ordinary Healing. Drakonite spells (Tempest, Annihilation, Meteor Strike, and White Mute) never combine, and neither do summons, the elemental Blast attacks, Ignis Fatuus, or physical attacks.

Spellbooks decide the element

A caster’s first equipped spellbook, including class-default equipment, sets the element ahead of any weapon, so a Book of Flame means Flame whatever the weapon. A plain Spellbook uses the caster’s own element. Without a spellbook, the first weapon supplies it if it has an element; otherwise the caster’s own element is used.

Find a recipe

Choose the spells your casters will actually cast. Add a third spell to see whether all three take part or the game keeps a pair.

Lightning

Lightning + Lightning forms a two-caster spell with a five-position cross.

The finder checks only whether the spells combine. Readiness, formation, the shared target, and the Unity check still apply.

Two-caster recipes

The game accepts 48 pairs, and caster order doesn’t matter. Within one element, T1 + T1 gives T1, while T1 + T2 and T2 + T2 give T2, and two T3 spells of the same element don’t combine.

Across elements, the compatible families are Wind + Flame, Wind + Water, Flame + Earth, Earth + Water, Wind + Bane, and Flame + Bane. A T3 spell works only with its exact T3 partner. A T2 + T2 pair covers nine positions, and every other pair covers a five-position cross.

Adding a third caster

A third caster can add power, change the result, or be left out entirely, so check the recipe before counting on all three. The game first sorts out the tiers:

Spell groups chosenWhat happens first
Three T1/T2 spellsAll three go on to the element check
One T3 and two T1/T2The T3 spell is left out
Two T3 and one T1/T2The T1/T2 spell is left out
Three T3 spellsAll three go on to the element check

Then it looks at elements. Casters of one element, or of a compatible pair of elements, can all stay. If three different elements remain, the game keeps its preferred pair, or none, and that pair still has to be an exact recipe.

Target area and power

The selected target is the centre of the spell’s area, which isn’t necessarily the centre of the enemy formation. Side positions are directly above, below, left, and right of it, and diagonal positions are the corners. Empty or out-of-bounds positions are skipped.

Power at each position

For each target, the game first works out every participating caster’s magic attack power against that target. It then arranges those powers into A, B, and C. With two casters, A is the higher power and B the lower.

With three casters there’s a bug. Call the first two casters’ powers lo and hi, lower first, and the third caster’s power Z:

Third power (Z)ABC
Z ≤ lohiloZ
lo < Z ≤ hiZlolo
Z > hiZhilo

In the middle case the highest power is dropped and the lowest counted twice. Powers of 78, 130, and 104, in that order, become A = 104, B = 78, and C = 78, for a total of 260 rather than 312. The recipe then decides how much power each position receives:

CombinationAreaSelected targetSide positionsDiagonals
Any pair except T2 + T2CrossA + B(A + B) ÷ 4—
T2 + T2 pairSquareA + BA + B ÷ 2(A + B) ÷ 2
Trio with fewer than two T2 spellsCrossA + B + C(A + B + C) ÷ 2—
Trio with two or more T2 spells, or three T3SquareA + B + CA + B + C ÷ 2(A + B + C) ÷ 2

Drop the fraction after each division. One unusual recipe, Acid Vapor + Ice Blast + Ice Field, makes Blue Spiral using the five-position trio rule; the recipe finder includes it.

These figures are the power reaching each position, not damage. Each target then subtracts its own magic defense and applies the Luck difference, resistance, and random multiplier as usual:

Damage = (combined power − magic defense + Luck difference)
× (100 − resistance) ÷ 100 × random multiplier
Drop the fraction, then keep the result between 1 and 9,999.

Luck is compared between the source caster and each target, including equipment Luck, and the other casters’ Luck isn’t added. A wider spell still has to get through each target’s own defense and resistance. Healing and status combinations follow their own rules; see Damage.

Worked example

Two Wizards in the middle row both use a plain Spellbook set to Flame. A Wizard uses T1 in that row, so each casts Fireball, and together they cast a combined Fireball, which has the same name but a five-position cross and much more power.

Each WizardValue
Magic Attack Coefficient53
INT / MEN / Luck55 / 61 / 50 (Wizard class values)
Equipment INTScipplay Staff +3, Spellbook +1, Amulet +4, for a total of +8; the Robe adds none
Condition+4 for a Flame spell from a Flame caster; fresh, Plain terrain, no row bonus
Two Wizards cast Fireball
Condition multiplier = (100 + 4) ÷ 100 = 1.04
Magic power = (53 + 8) ÷ 6 × (55 + 50) ÷ 50 × (61 + 100) ÷ 100 × 1.04
= 35.7, dropped to 35 per Wizard
 
Selected target: 35 + 35 = 70
Side positions: 70 ÷ 4 = 17.5, dropped to 17

The target is the level-1 Amazon from the Damage example: MEN 48 plus 2 from her Bandanna, INT 45, Magic Defense Coefficient 23, and Flame resistance 50, with equal Luck.

Damage to an Amazon, random multiplier 1.00
Magic defense = 23 ÷ 20 × (48 + 2 + 25) ÷ 25 × (45 + 100) ÷ 100 = 5.0, dropped to 5
 
As the selected target: (70 − 5) × 0.50 = 32.5, so 32 HP
In a side position: (17 − 5) × 0.50 = 6 HP

An Amazon takes one of these, depending on where she stands. Side damage isn’t a quarter of 32, because the power is reduced before her defense is subtracted. Unity decided only whether the combination happened, and it didn’t change the 70 or the 17.

When a combination doesn’t happen

CheckWhat to look for
SpellsLook at the spells actually being cast, not the class names or weapons.
RecipeUse the finder. Some three-caster choices leave one caster out on purpose.
TargetThe casters must pick the same target. Try Attack Leader if they split.
ReadinessA sleeping, paralyzed, or delayed caster drops out.
FormationKeep the casters together. Exactly which positions work is still unknown.
UnityBelow Unity 99, even a perfect setup can fail the check.

Unity glossary

Unity

A number shared by a whole squad that sets the chance of passing the combined-spell check. It doesn’t make the spell stronger and isn’t spent when a combination succeeds.

Unity check

The roll a squad must pass before its casters can combine. The game rolls 0–99, and the check passes if the roll is equal to or below the squad’s Unity.

Combined spell

A single spell made from two or three casters’ spells. Their actual spells must form a recipe, they must share a target, and the squad must pass its Unity check.

T1, T2, and T3

This guide’s names for the three spell groups a class can use in a formation row. They aren’t character levels. The class and row choose the group, and equipment chooses its element.

Actual spell

The spell a caster really casts once their class, formation row, and equipment are taken into account. Recipes check this spell, not the caster’s class.

Recipe

An exact set of compatible spells and the combined spell it produces. Being one of the 17 compatible spells doesn’t mean a spell combines with every other one.

Shared target

The target every participating caster has chosen. The casters must agree on it, and the squad’s tactic affects whether they do.

Flag of Unity

An item that adds 1–5 Unity to a squad, up to 100. It isn’t sold in any ordinary shop.

Spellbook priority

For a standard elemental spell group, a caster’s first equipped spellbook sets the element before any weapon can. A plain Spellbook uses the caster’s own element.

Three-caster combination

A combination in which all three spells survive the recipe checks. Its power can be lower than expected because of a bug that sometimes drops the highest caster’s power.

Third caster left out

When three casters try to combine but only two of their spells form a recipe, the game keeps that pair. Only the pair contributes, and the pair’s area and power rules apply.

Selected target

The position the spell is aimed at. It is the centre of the spell’s area and receives the most power. It doesn’t have to be the centre of the enemy formation.

Side position

A position directly above, below, left, or right of the selected target. How much power it receives depends on the recipe.

Diagonal position

One of the four corner positions around the selected target. Only nine-position spells reach them.

A — first power

The first caster power after the game arranges them. In a pair, A is the higher power. With three casters, a bug can leave the highest power out.

B — second power

The second caster power after the game arranges them. In a pair, B is the lower power.

C — third power

The third caster power after the game arranges them. Because of a bug, it can be a copy of the lowest power. In a pair, C is zero.

Combined power

The power that reaches one target position, worked out from the casters’ powers and the recipe’s area rule. It goes into the ordinary magic damage formula, so it isn’t damage yet.

Source caster

The caster whose Luck is compared with each target’s in the damage calculation. The other casters’ Luck isn’t added in.

Modder reference: Unity and combined spells

A combined spell passes three separate stages. First the Unity check decides whether an attempt starts. Next, three small lookup tables decide which casters stay and what spell they make. Finally, a power routine combines the casters’ powers, and that routine has a bug in its three-caster case. The recipe tables are uncompressed ROM data, and Unity itself is one byte per squad.

Where these facts come from

Every location and value on this tab was read from the US retail ROM, and offsets are z64. The recipe catalog was checked by replaying all 969 three-spell and 153 two-spell choices through a re-implementation of the lookup code. None of the suggested edits has been tried in a running game yet.

What do you want to change?

Make combinations happen more or less often

Change the Unity comparison, or how Unity is gained. Recipes and readiness still apply afterwards.

See Unity check

Add or change a recipe

Edit the output trie. The two selector tries decide which casters survive before the output is chosen.

See Recipe tables · How the tries are read

Fix the three-caster power bug

The bug is in code, not in the recipe tables.

See Three-caster power bug

How to read the code and byte evidence

ROM offsets use big-endian z64 order. The master v64 stores each byte pair in reverse order. RAM addresses belong to the stated overlay or structure.

Each code line shows the z64 offset, the four original bytes, and the MIPS instruction. Relative branches name z64 destinations; J/JAL targets are encoded RAM addresses. The instruction after a branch is its delay slot.

Samples are stored bytes, not calculated values. For compressed resources, the sample gives the container’s ROM offset and the offset inside the decoded file.

Unity checkRecipe tablesHow the tries are readThree-caster power bug

Unity check

The combined-spell resolver compares PRNG() % 100 with the squad’s Unity and rejects the attempt when the roll is higher. Unity 50 therefore passes on 51 of 100 rolls, and Unity 99 always passes. This check runs before the participant and recipe checks finish, so passing it guarantees nothing.

Code
func_0022F580, comparison at z64 0x0022F634–0x0022F67C.
Writers
Flag of Unity adds a random 1–5, capped at 100. One battle-results path adds 5, capped at 99. Removing an ordinary member sets 0.
Not affected
No reader scales damage, healing, or anything else by Unity.

How to change it

To set a squad’s Unity, write byte +0x0C of its 25-byte squad record in RAM. To make every attempt pass, the comparison in this function would need patching.

Watch out for

  • The saved record (+0x0C) and the active squad (+0x1F) hold copies of the same value; change the one in use.
  • The save stores 7 bits, so 0–127 fits, but values above 100 aren’t produced by the game.

Recipe tables

Three tries decide a combination. The game sorts the spells by tier, and the tier trie returns a mask of which to keep. It re-sorts the survivors by element, and the element trie returns another mask. Finally, the survivors’ spell codes, sorted, are looked up in the output trie, which returns the result spell and the area rule.

Element trie
z64 0x008AC4C6, 4-byte records: key, kept-mask result, and child offset (u16). The first records are 01 00 00 1A 02 00 00 78 03 00 00 C0 04 00 00 EE.
Tier trie
z64 0x008AC5F6, same format. The first records are 01 00 00 0E 03 00 00 3A 05 00 00 54 FF 00 01 03.
Output trie
z64 0x008AC656, 6-byte records: key, output code, area rule, a byte, and child offset (u16). FF means no result.
End marker
A key of FF ends a list of siblings.

How to change it

To change what an existing pair makes, find its path in the output trie and change the output code (and area rule). New recipes need new records. The tables are packed back to back, so adding a leaf means moving later records and fixing every child offset, or relocating the table.

Watch out for

  • Child offsets are relative to each table’s own base.
  • A recipe also needs both spells to survive the tier and element tries.

How the tries are read

The readers walk siblings until a key matches, then jump to that record’s child list. A nonzero result is remembered as the walk continues, so a longer path that ends in zero keeps the last nonzero result. A flat list of (pair → result) would miss this behaviour.

Code
func_00210730 (element), func_0021079C (tier), and func_00210820 (output and shared reader), with the reader at z64 0x00210844–0x00210880.
Output
For the output trie, an area rule other than FF is also remembered along the path.

Watch out for

  • When editing, re-run a full catalog check. The project’s verify-unity.cjs replays every choice through these rules.

Three-caster power bug

After working out each caster’s power against a target, the routine orders the first two as hi and lo. For the third power Z, it should produce a proper sort. When lo < Z ≤ hi, it instead produces (Z, lo, lo), which drops hi and counts lo twice. Powers 78, 130, 104 become 104, 78, 78.

Code
func_00239338, the overwrite at z64 0x00239524–0x00239560.
Other cases
Z ≤ lo gives (hi, lo, Z); Z > hi gives (Z, hi, lo). Both are correct.
Luck
The acting caster still supplies Luck; the rearrangement doesn’t change which caster that is.

How to change it

Fixing the bug means changing the middle case’s stores to produce (hi, Z, lo). It changes retail behaviour, so test it on healing trios as well as damage.

Watch out for

  • The recipe tables can’t work around this; it’s code.

COMBAT SYSTEMS

Battle turns, rows, and tactics

How many times each class attacks from each row, which enemy your squad aims at, and how the game decides who won.

When two squads meet, every character gets a set number of attacks decided by their class and their row in the formation, plus one more when a Princess leads the squad. The squad’s tactic chooses targets. When the attacks run out, the side with the only survivors wins; if both sides still stand, the side that took less damage wins.

How a battle plays out

  • Row sets the attack. Each class has a front-row, middle-row, and back-row attack, each used a set number of times.
  • Tactics set the target. The same tactic applies to the whole squad.
  • Front rows strike first, and speed decides the rest. Each side works from its front row back, and the faster row goes first.
  • Damage taken decides close fights. If both sides survive, the side that lost less HP wins.

Attacks by row

Each class uses one attack per row, a set number of times. Moving a character to another row can change the attack, the count, or both. Spells marked T1, T2, or T3 depend on the caster’s equipment; see Which spell each caster uses.
